evidence.mechanism: shot-08s: six symmetric arms on the lattice axes, each with regular comb side-branches spaced along its length; by shot-20s the side arms feather out with varying lengths, but no visible tip or lag defect.
evidence.ambition: shot-08s: one flat fill layer with a subtle radial vignette, no lighting or material; the branching is a single shape pass. by shot-20s the same layer is denser, using under a third of the 12 KB budget.
evidence.craft: shot-02s: text fragments clipped at the frame edges and stray letter debris along the top-left arms; by shot-08s the rose-clay ground and oxblood arms are clean, with crisp edges and no moire.
evidence.distinctness: shot-08s: a centred oxblood six-arm snowflake on rose-clay, a motif many demos have used; the recent Penrose night is ochre and rust on cream with a tiling, so palette and layout differ from it.
evidence.polish: shot-02s: figure sits in the left half with its text clipped at the frame edges; by shot-20s the figure is centred, mirrored and resolved, with arms of differing lengths.

pairwise_justification: shot-08s shows one sparse six-arm figure on flat rose; the 2026-11-23 Penrose strip grows from one kite into a dense ochre and rust tiling, so the median wins the head-to-head.

critique.change: Add a second rendering idea: shade each arm with a lit ridge highlight and a darker underside, and give the back arms a lower-contrast depth layer so the figure reads as a 3D crystal rather than one flat fill.
Make the fixed-lag rule visible: draw a bright growth tip at the front and birth each side branch at a constant distance behind it, so early arms stop short at 8s and late arms keep extending to 20s.
Clean the craft flaws: remove the clipped text and stray letter debris at shot-02s, and centre the tip so the 2s frame is composed rather than cut at the left edge.
